thread.title: Looking for a job in 2019 with no tech skills? Don’t rule out Google, Apple or Amazon

author: Kari Paul
title: Looking for a job in 2019 with no tech skills? Don’t rule out Google, Apple or Amazon
text:
By many measures, it’s never been a better time to be part of the American workforce.
The job market in the U.S. is booming — with unemployment at a 49-year low of 3%. That means 2019 is a great time to look for work, according to the 2019 Job Market Trends Report released Tuesday by recruiting company Glassdoor.
“If anyone is not satisfied in their career, now is the time to start looking for a new job,” Glassdoor chief economist Andrew Chamberlain said. “Job seekers are currently in the driver’s seat for the best pay and benefits.”
Here are trends job seekers can look forward to in the year ahead:
You don’t have to be an engineer to get a tech job Demand for non-tech workers, even at tech companies, will be on the rise, the Glassdoor report found. That means companies like Amazon AMZN, -4.46% and Apple AAPL, -0.93% will have more roles like sales jobs in need of employees. In fact, more than half of the new roles at Amazon’s proposed headquarters in New York City will not be tech-focused , the company said in November.
“In the early days of startups, most jobs were engineering roles, but as companies grow they need to generate revenue,” Chamberlain said. “This is important because a lot of non-tech workers want to find a way to get into the tech industry and be in a fast-growing dynamic sector.”
This also means more jobs at major tech companies will be opening up in cities outside of major hubs like San Francisco, the Glassdoor report added. Apple AAPL, -0.93% announced last week that it would be building a new campus in Austin, Texas and Google GOOG, -2.45% announced an expansion of thousands of new jobs to New York City.
Aging workforce creates opportunity By 2025, there will be more retirees in America than children under the age of 18, according to the U.S. Census. The aging workforce means more job openings for young employees to fill, the latest report said “Like a slowly rising tide, these demographic changes will have wide-ranging impacts on jobs, pay and hiring in the future,” the report concluded, but may also mean a potential talent shortage for higher-skilled jobs.
Negotiate, negotiate, negotiate With the labor market on the worker’s side, every employee should negotiate, Chamberlain said. And negotiating rarely hurts: In fact, 19% of recruiters said the salary negotiation had a positive impact on their decision to hire the candidate, according to a November survey from recruiting platform Jobvite, and 43% said it had no impact on their decision to hire. Just 10% reported that they did not offer the job after the candidate negotiated their salary.
Rachel Bitte, chief people officer at Jobvite, said you should know your true market value. “Go into any salary negotiation without knowing the facts, and you run the risk of botching the whole process.”
Employees should always negotiate salary, Chamberlain said, but other benefits are up for discussion as well. Although eye-catching perks like workout benefits, in-office snacks, and even free car washes for employees have been on the rise, it’s important to ask for traditional benefits, he said. Negotiate for more paid time off, better 401(k) matching, and health insurance that works for you.
Data privacy is a new frontier of workers’ rights After a year of major data breaches, the conversation around how to protect customer data is heating up — but employees need data protection, too, the Glassdoor report said.
Companies regularly collect sensitive data like Social Security Numbers, health-care information, and addresses from employees. They also collect other personal information through surveys or even through location-tracking if employees work in transportation, the report showed.
“Workers should be asking what data employers are collecting and what are the rules around how that data is kept,” Chamberlain said. “They really need to take control.” Do they want you to wear a Fitbit? You may not regard that as part of your job description.
